function localParts(iso: string): { date: string; time: string } | undefined {
  const ms = Date.parse(iso);
  if (isNaN(ms)) return undefined;
  const m: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const p of fmt.formatToParts(new Date(ms))) m[p.type] = p.value;

  const inScope = items.filter((it) => {
    const d = localDate(it.recorded);

content.text:
The revised mapper is in `out/transform.ts`. It type-checks and runs on the samples. I couldn't reproduce the four missing allergy rows, so the fix is a best guess at the cause.

The feedback listed no items, and the 8 samples only have "NKDA" allergy entries. The earlier mapper read allergies only from the latest document that had any. My guess is that a later document's allergy list sometimes omits or replaces a real allergy that an earlier document lists, for example lisinopril or dapagliflozin. That would explain a row expected but missing.

Two changes:
- **Allergies are combined across documents.** The mapper now collects allergies from every current document (not superseded or retracted, on or before `asOf`) and keys them by substance. Where a substance appears more than once, the latest entry wins. "NKDA" is still skipped.
- **One row per substance.** A drug that appears both on the allergy list and as a T-code adverse-effect diagnosis now gives one row, not two.

The trade-off is that an allergy a later document deliberately removed would still be reported. The schema has no "inactive" flag on allergies, so I couldn't tell that case apart from a document that simply left the entry out.
